Clean body weight records

Source: R/clean_weight.R
clean_weight.Rd

Flag implausible and outlying body weight records, then decide for each pig whether its weight data are good enough for growth analysis.

Usage

clean_weight(visits, qc = qc_config(), verbose = 1)

Arguments

visits

Visit table from prep_visits().

qc

QC settings from qc_config(). Used here: weight_range, weight_outlier, outlier_combine, rlm_cutoff, sd_max, loess_span, rel_dev_max, daily_drop_min, min_records, min_test_days, max_missing_rate, entry_weight_max, exit_weight_min, curve_r2_min.

verbose

0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details).

Value

An object of class ppt_weight (a list):

  • per_pig: one row per pig with n_records, n_valid, n_outliers, first_date, last_date, test_days, missing_rate, entry_weight, exit_weight (kg, from the fitted curve), r2, status ("keep", "low_confidence" or "removed") and reason;

  • daily: one row per pig and day for pigs not removed: median of the valid weights (weight, kg), n_records, n_outliers;

  • records: every weight record with fitted, outlier and qc_flag (why it was flagged);

  • removed: pigs removed here, plus misreads logged by prep_visits();

  • settings: the QC settings used.

Details

Pig checks use the valid (non-outlier) records only:

  • n_valid < min_records, test_days < min_test_days or missing_rate > max_missing_rate (share of test days without a valid weight) remove the pig;

  • entry_weight > entry_weight_max, exit_weight < exit_weight_min or r2 < curve_r2_min mark the pig "low_confidence" but keep it: its growth can still be estimated by extrapolation in calc_adg(), with a flag.

See also

prep_visits() for the previous step, qc_config() for the settings.

Examples

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits)
#> 
#> ── Cleaning body weight (rlm) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Weight records: 31,472
#> • Outside weight range: 0
#> • Outliers: 2,975
#> ! Pigs kept: 28, low confidence: 1, removed: 1
w
#> 
#> ── <ppt_weight> ──
#> 
#> Pigs: 30 (keep 28, low confidence 1, removed 1)
#> $per_pig: 30 rows x 14 columns
#> $daily: 2789 rows x 7 columns
#> $removed: 1 row x 4 columns
#> $records: 31472 rows x 9 columns
#> QC profile: "casey"

# Why pigs were removed
w$removed
#>    responder location         step                 reason
#>       <char>   <char>       <char>                 <char>
#> 1:     15964      101 clean_weight test period 2 d < 35 d

# Records flagged as outliers
head(w$records[outlier == TRUE])
#>    responder location       date seq_days          entry_time weight   fitted
#>       <char>   <char>     <Date>    <int>              <POSc>  <num>    <num>
#> 1:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 01:05:04   31.0 21.48760
#> 2:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 06:52:21   28.5 21.69242
#> 3:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 06:53:50   29.5 21.69330
#> 4:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 08:46:55   30.0 21.76008
#> 5:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 11:28:05   29.5 21.85532
#> 6:     13913      101 2024-02-20        2 2024-02-20 11:32:56   27.5 21.85819
#>    outlier qc_flag
#>     <lgcl>  <char>
#> 1:    TRUE     rlm
#> 2:    TRUE     rlm
#> 3:    TRUE     rlm
#> 4:    TRUE     rlm
#> 5:    TRUE     rlm
#> 6:    TRUE     rlm

# Another QC preset
w_national <- clean_weight(visits, qc = qc_config("national"), verbose = 0)
table(w_national$per_pig$status)
#> 
#>           keep low_confidence        removed 
#>             26              3              1
